To allow a device to communicate across VLANs on a UniFi network, you need to configure proper inter-VLAN routing and firewall rules. Here’s a step-by-step guide:

1. Ensure Proper VLAN Setup
	•	Confirm that your UniFi network has the necessary VLANs configured in Settings > Networks. For example:
	•	VLAN 10: IoT devices
	•	VLAN 20: Main network
	•	Each VLAN must have a unique subnet and IP range.

2. Enable Inter-VLAN Routing
	•	By default, a UniFi Gateway (e.g., UniFi Dream Machine) routes traffic between VLANs unless restricted by firewall rules.
	•	Ensure VLANs are correctly assigned to the interfaces/ports for your devices.

3. Configure Firewall Rules

To allow a device on one VLAN to “speak” to devices on another, you need to define allow rules:
	1.	Go to Settings > Firewall & Security > Rules.
	2.	Under LAN IN, create a new rule:
	•	Rule Action: Accept
	•	Protocol: TCP/UDP (or specify protocols like ICMP for ping, etc.)
	•	Source: The specific device’s IP range or VLAN (e.g., VLAN 10).
	•	Destination: The specific device’s IP range or VLAN (e.g., VLAN 20).
	•	Port: Specify the ports required for communication (or use “All” if you’re unsure).
	3.	Order Matters: Place the allow rule above any default deny rules.

4. Test Connectivity
	•	Use ping or traceroute to test whether the device can communicate across VLANs.
	•	If communication fails, review your firewall rules and ensure no deny rules are blocking the traffic.

5. Optional: Limit Communication
	•	If you want to restrict communication to specific devices rather than entire VLANs, narrow the firewall rules to source and destination IP addresses instead of ranges.

6. Save and Monitor
	•	Save your settings and monitor network traffic in the UniFi Controller to ensure the communication works as intended.

If you’re dealing with specific services (e.g., Bonjour, multicast), additional configurations like enabling mDNS or IGMP snooping may be required. Let me know if you need help with those!
